title: midyear-service-signal-and-priority-huddle-jun-29-2026
content:
Purpose: quick sync to align SRE + Platform teams on mid‑year service signals, immediate reliability priorities, and followups from the June incidents. Informal notes, action items, and owners. Treat as working doc; will convert to playbook updates after signoff.

Attendees (quick call): Marisol (SRE lead), Kenji (infra), Priya (monitoring), Ethan (serving runtime), Sofia (oncall rotations), 14 attendees total (see Slack thread #sre-midyear-huddle).

Agenda:
- 5m: TL;DR of June service blips and root causes
- 10m: Current signal coverage gaps (alerts, dashboards, SLO blindspots)
- 10m: Immediate mitigations (next 30 days) and owners
- 10m: Roadmap items that reduce blast radius (Q3/Q4)
- 10m: Open questions and quick decisions (oncall, runbooks, and runbook drills)

Notes and context:
- June 18th spike (incident ENG-3421): brief recap — upstream autoscaler misconfiguration + an unexpected codec fallback increased per-request CPU and pushed some Dedicated hosts into OOM churn. No customer-facing data loss, but elevated 5xx and throttling for 18m.
- Root cause identified: autoscaler threshold not accounting for runtime-side batching CPU overhead at 1.5x typical token rates. Also we lacked a fast-fail alert for sustained host OOM cycles.
- Observed metrics during the window: P50 latency +12ms, P95 +110ms, error rate 0.8% -> peak 3.5% in affected pool. Token throughput dropped ~18% while autoscaler tried to reacquire capacity.

Signal coverage gaps (prioritized list):
1) Host-level OOM cycles: no durable counter alert. Current alert only fires on single OOM event; need an aggregate over 5m with rate and host-flap filter. (owner: Kenji)
2) Runtime batching CPU skew: no early-warning for sudden delta between requested tokens/sec and observed CPU per-token. Create derived metric cpu_per_token moving-average. (owner: Priya)
3) Cross-pool fallback visibility: when routing falls back to lower-cost pool, we don't tag traffic in traces consistently. Add tag at routing layer. (owner: Ethan)
4) Canary degradation SLOs: canary checks exist but are too coarse for tail latency shifts. Add synthetic tail checks for critical endpoints. (owner: Sofia)

Immediate (30-day) mitigations (MUST ship):
- Create OOM-flap alert (rule + runbook) that triggers when host OOM count > 3 in 5m or when host restart rate exceeds 0.5 restarts/min. Triage path: page SRE, escalate to infra. JIRA: ENG-3499. (Kenji; due 2026-07-12)
- Short-term autoscaler tuning: adjust scale-up threshold to include CPU-per-pod 95th percentile under high-batch scenarios; add a conservative rate-limit to prevent simultaneous upscales on startup. (Ethan + Kenji; due 2026-07-08)
- Add cpu_per_token derived metric and dashboard tile in PROD: visualize by model family + sequence length bucket. (Priya; due 2026-07-05)
- Temporary routing guard: when pool hit ratio exceeds 85% and P95 > target, stop automatic fallbacks for 10m and run manual escalation. (Marisol; runbook update due 2026-07-01)

Roadmap items (Q3/Q4, lower risk, but impactful):
- Prefill vs live-batch profiling: invest in a profiler that distinguishes prefill CPU costs vs autoregressive token costs for each model variant — will reduce model-level surprises and improve autoscaler heuristics. (owner: Applied ML + Ethan; planning ticket ENG-3615)
- KV cache durability improvements to reduce OOM during cold-cache storms (design doc in progress). (owner: serving-runtime)
- Gradual rollout pipeline for autoscaler config changes with automated rollback and canary traffic split. (owner: platform-engineering)

Operational housekeeping & decisions:
- Oncall rotation: proposal to trial 12-hour oncall windows for infra SRE (instead of 24h) for July only to reduce fatigue. Vote: tentative yes -> trial starts 2026-07-06. (Sofia to publish schedule)
- Runbook drills: mandatory 1x/month for all SREs + 1x/quarter cross-team for platform + serving runtime. Next drill: July 20th, scenario = progressive OOM cascade. (Marisol)
- Postmortem cadence: for sev2+ incidents, owner must open postmortem within 72h and link to ticket. Use template in Confluence (Signal-Playbook).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we freeze any autoscaler tuning changes while infra ticket ENG-3401 (cloud provider instance-type migration) is ongoing? Risk: conflicting instance sizes might negate tuning. Proposal: hold major topology changes until migration is in canary (expected 2026-08-15). Vote: agree.
- Should we roll out the cpu_per_token metric to Dedicated customers' dashboards? Operationally possible but could leak internal signals; for now surface to internal only. Review in 60 days.

Action items (short list):
- Kenji: ENG-3499 create OOM-flap alert + runbook (due 2026-07-12)
- Priya: implement cpu_per_token metric + basic dashboard (due 2026-07-05)
- Ethan: patch autoscaler tuning PR + integration test (due 2026-07-08) -> link PR: git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra#PR-982
- Marisol: update routing runbook and publish temporary fallback guard (due 2026-07-01)
- Sofia: publish July oncall trial schedule and coordinate July 20 runbook drill (due 2026-07-02)

Notes to self / rough brainstorm (fragmented):
- Consider short-term circuit-breaker for model families that create high tail variance (cheap to add at routing layer).
- Investigate using trace sampling that biases toward recently restarted hosts to catch OOM-induced errors faster.
- Build a simple smoke test that runs after autoscaler config changes to ensure no immediate host churn.

Attachments / references:
- Incident deck (internal): link pinned in #sre-midyear-huddle Slack thread
- Monitoring playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Signal-Playbook
- Triage checklist: doc attached to ENG-3421 JIRA

Final notes: this doc is intentionally terse; capture immediate priorities and owners so we can convert to playbook updates. Expect follow-ups in the next 7 days from owners above. If you have objections to any owner assignments, reply in-thread in Slack or add a comment here.

-- Marisol
